toneRules: Editorial, not salesy. Write like a thoughtful editor: short sentences, real examples, no jargon soup.
Confident, not cocky. No superlatives. The product does the work, so quiet confidence reads stronger than 'world-class'.
Precise, not vague. 'Writes three posts a week' beats 'boosts productivity'. Concrete always wins.
Show receipts rather than claims. Name the actual thing that happened.
Stay human. Write for a person, not a persona. Admitting what is still rough is on-brand.
Never use an em-dash (—) in copy. In 2026 it reads as machine-written. Use a comma, a parenthesis, or a full stop. A spaced en-dash as a German Gedankenstrich is fine.
Light and warm, not corporate. Paper is the ground; deep purple is a detail colour, not a field.
voice.narrationStyle: Warm, credible, founder-to-founder. Conversational and restrained, crisp articulation, natural micro-pauses. No hype, no radio-announcer tone, no rising sell.
voice.narratorRegister: one man, low-to-mid register, speaking pitch around 140 hertz

do: Let paper carry the frame. Cream and white do the heavy lifting; yellow is the one thing the eye lands on.
Use deep purple for headline type, structure and detail, and only rarely as a full field.
Set headlines in DM Serif Display and labels in JetBrains Mono. The contrast between them is the identity.
Reserve the yellow highlight for one phrase per frame. It is earned, not given.
Carry one continuous element through the whole piece so it reads as one thought.
Set the brand as lowercase 'my' in the sans and 'HERALD' in the serif.
Show the real product where it proves a point.
dont: Never invent a product interface. With no real screenshot, stay conceptual.
Never make deep purple the default ground for every scene. Since v1.1 the inverse field is punctuation, not layout: roughly one scene in six, not five in six.
Never centre every scene, and never repeat a layout in adjacent scenes.
Never use a colour outside the palette, and never introduce a second accent.
Never stretch, rotate, outline or recolour the logo.
Never state a number that no approved fact backs.
Never imply anything publishes without a human approving it.
